title: Origins of the US remote viewing program with Puthoff, Targ and Swann
summary: Lyn Buchanan tells of Origins of the US remote viewing program with Puthoff, Targ and Swann, about 1960s-1970s at United States (no place named), and summarises it without a named source. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: They contacted Ingo Swan. Ingo Swan developed the methodology called controlled remote viewing. They started a remote viewing unit and that unit had been in existence 10 years before I got there.

plain: A former Army sergeant named Lyn Buchanan tells podcast host Jesse Michels how the US government's remote viewing programme began, remote viewing being the claimed ability to describe distant places or things using only the mind. He says researchers including Hal Puthoff and Russell Targ contacted a man named Ingo Swann, who developed a method called controlled remote viewing, and that a military remote viewing unit was formed and had run for ten years before Buchanan joined it. If true, it would mean the government took psychic abilities seriously enough to fund them for years.
